executiveSummary: A fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad killed 14 newborns on Wednesday, August 26, 2026. The incident has triggered a government investigation, public outrage, and conflicting accounts regarding the cause of the blaze and the response of hospital staff and emergency services. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has ordered an inquiry and suspended the federal health secretary.

timeline.dateSource: It was 6:30am on Wednesday when Arif Rana, 46, woke to a phone call.
timeline.description: A fire erupts in the maternity ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad.

timeline.dateSource: According to hospital management, the fire was caused by a short circuit in the nursery’s air-conditioning unit.
timeline.description: Hospital management identifies the cause of the fire as a short circuit in the air-conditioning unit.

timeline.dateSource: The nursery had 15 newborns in it at the time. Only one was rescued.
timeline.description: Hospital officials report that 15 newborns were in the nursery and only one was rescued.

timeline.dateSource: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ordered an investigation into the fire and later suspended the federal health secretary, Aslam Ghaury.
timeline.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif orders an investigation and suspends the federal health secretary.

timeline.dateSource: Investigators appointed by Pakistan's prime minister were making a visit Thursday to the hospital nursery where a fast-moving fire killed 14 newborns
timeline.description: A high-level investigation committee, led by retired federal secretary Shahid Khan, visits the nursery to gather statements and determine the cause of the fire.

timeline.dateSource: In its preliminary report, however, the hospital said a blast involving a nebulizer sparked the blaze
timeline.description: The hospital's preliminary report contradicts its earlier statement, attributing the fire to a blast involving a nebulizer.

significance.reasoning: The incident is a significant tragedy within Pakistan, resulting in the deaths of 14 newborns and prompting a government investigation. The reporting highlights systemic issues with hospital safety and emergency response. While it is a major local event, it does not appear to have immediate global geopolitical implications.

entities.role: Islamabad's largest public-sector hospital where the fire occurred.

entities.name: Arif Rana
entities.role: A witness who rushed to the maternity ward to rescue his sister and her newborn.

entities.role: Ordered an investigation into the fire and suspended the federal health secretary.

entities.name: Aslam Ghaury
entities.role: Federal health secretary who was suspended by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

entities.role: Retired federal secretary leading the investigation committee appointed by the Prime Minister.

entities.name: Maryam Nawaz
entities.role: Punjab's Chief Minister who ordered the arrest of the medical superintendent and three senior doctors after a previous fire in June 2024.

sources.bias: The reporting combines detailed, on-the-ground witness accounts from Al Jazeera with official statements from hospital management and government officials. The conflicting information regarding the cause of the fire and the timeline of the emergency call indicates a need to verify claims from multiple sources.
